title_en: Watching the Fire from Across the River
full_text_zh:
[P1] 隔岸观火

[P2] 清晨，赵国都城邯郸的城门刚刚打开一条缝，一人一马就飞驰而来。
"让开！让开！"马上的人大叫着，一刻不停地往前冲。城门口的人赶紧让出一条路，让他纵马穿过，直向王宫奔去！
让开！
让开！

[P3] "唉，一定又打败仗了！"路边的百姓都唉声叹气。前不久，赵国和秦国在长平大战一场。赵国45万大军上阵，只有240个人活着回来。邯郸城中，几乎每家每户都有男子战死，城里天天哭声不断。

[P4] “报！秦国武安君白起领兵，已经攻下17座城了，正快速向邯郸袭来！”传令官慌慌张张地向赵王禀报。赵王急得像热锅上的蚂蚁——团团转。这可如何是好？等到白起围住邯郸城，赵国可就要完蛋了。

[P5] 赵王紧急召唤大臣们来商议，大臣们也是抓耳挠腮，想不出好办法。白起是秦国百战百胜的“战神”，赵国没有将领能打得过他呀！平原君的门客苏代是个口才好、智谋多的人。这时候，苏代向赵王献计说：“我愿意冒死去秦国，凭我这三寸不烂之舌，说动秦国退兵。”

[P6] 苏代带着许多金银财宝来到了秦国。秦国的国君秦昭王，文拜范雎为丞相，武用白起为将军，将秦国治理得越来越强大。可是，苏代却没有去求见秦昭王，请他从赵国退兵，而是带着贵重的礼物，来到了范雎的丞相府。他想做什么呢？

[P7] 苏代向范雎行了个礼说：‘白起在长平大胜，威风凛凛，如果再打下邯郸，就是秦国统一天下的头号功臣了！’范雎一听他这话，脸色就黑了下来。苏代一点也不怕，接着说道：‘我真为丞相您担心呀！您现在的官位虽然比白起高，可是过不了多久，白起就在您之上了。’

[P8] 范雎心里很不服气，虽然他没有上战场，但是征收粮草，出谋划策，他的功劳也不小呀，白起的官位怎么能比他高呢？
过了好一会儿，他才问苏代：“你有什么好办法？”苏代送上他带来的礼物，说：“丞相为什么不劝秦王从邯郸退兵，跟赵国议和呢？这样白起就不能再立功劳，您的地位就稳如泰山了。”

[P9] 第二天，范雎就对秦王说："大王，长平之战，我们死伤不少人，不如两国先停战，让赵国割让几座城池给我们。我们的士兵打了几年仗，太累了，让他们回来休整休整吧！"秦王想了想说："连年征战，我们储存的粮草也不多了，这时候停战也好！"他同意了议和，收下赵国献出的六座城池后，就让白起领兵回咸阳。赵国也就得救了。

[P10] 此时，白起正想一鼓作气打下赵国呢！突然接到撤兵的命令，他只好怒气冲冲地回到了咸阳城。听说是范雎提出要议和，白起就对他吹胡子瞪眼，非常讨厌他。

[P11] 停战这一年风调雨顺。秋天的时候，秦国的庄稼丰收了，兵器战车也都修好了。于是，秦王又想让白起带兵攻打赵国。白起正生着病呢，却还是进宫劝秦王：‘我们撤兵后，赵国派使者带着礼物，跟各个诸侯国结了盟。现在他们联合起来，正防范着我们秦国呢，这场仗打不赢呀！’

[P12] 秦王知道，白起从邯郸撤兵后，心里一直不高兴。他以为白起是故意装病，不肯去打仗，便气呼呼地说："你白起不愿意领兵怕什么，我秦国的将领多着呢！"于是，他派了另一员大将王陵去打赵国。没想到，王陵打仗真不行，不但没能打胜仗，连自己的军营都被赵军攻破了。

[P13] 秦王又派范雎去请白起出战。白起看到范雎，火冒三丈："长平之战，我们杀了45万赵军，赵国人被吓破了胆。那正是灭掉赵国的好机会，你却劝大王跟赵国议和。现在赵国加高了城墙，挖深了护城河，扩充了军队……他们军民一心，怎么打得下来？我的病还没有好呢，打不了仗！"
哼！

[P14] 范雎回到王宫，把白起的话原原本本地告诉了秦王。秦王一听，怒不可遏，马上下了诏书：削去白起的官爵，降为士兵，全族搬出咸阳城。白起生病走不了，秦王便给他限时三个月。三个月时间一到，秦王就天天派人来赶白起。

[P15] 十二月的咸阳城，寒风呼呼地刮着，白起带着两个随从，悄悄从西门出了咸阳城。范雎听说后，又担忧地对秦王说：‘白起心里肯定怨恨大王，如果他离开咸阳，投奔了别国，那就会成为咱们秦国的祸害呀！’秦王一听，立刻派快马追上白起，赐给他一把锋利的宝剑。

[P16] 白起围攻邯郸的时候，苏代来到秦国，挑起范雎的妒忌之火，让他与白起内斗。范雎成功劝秦王从邯郸撤了兵，这才解了赵国的燃眉之急，使赵国免遭灭亡。赵国静观敌人自相残杀，就像站在岸边看对岸失火一样，什么也不用做，最后还能从中得到好处，这样的计策，就叫“隔岸观火”。
full_text_en:
[P1] Watching the Fire from the Other Side of the River

[P2] In the morning, the city gate of Handan, the capital of the State of Zhao, had just opened a crack, and a man on horseback galloped through.
"Make way! Make way!" shouted the man on horseback, charging forward without stopping. The people at the city gate quickly made a path, letting him ride through and head straight for the royal palace!
Make way!
Make way!

[P3] "Ah, we've lost again!" The people by the roadside sighed in despair. Not long ago, Zhao and Qin fought a great battle at Changping. Zhao's 450,000-strong army went into battle, but only 240 men returned alive. In Handan, almost every household had lost a man to war, and the city echoed with constant weeping.

[P4] "Report! General Bai Qi of Qin has led his troops and already captured 17 cities, advancing rapidly toward Handan!" The messenger, flustered, reported to King Zhao. The King of Zhao was frantic, like an ant on a hot pan—going in circles. What could be done? Once Bai Qi surrounds Handan, the State of Zhao will be doomed.

[P5] King Zhao urgently summoned his ministers to discuss the situation, but the ministers were scratching their heads, unable to come up with a good plan. Bai Qi was the 'war god' of Qin, undefeated in hundreds of battles; no general of Zhao could defeat him! Su Dai, a guest of Pingyuan Jun, was a man with excellent eloquence and much wisdom. At this moment, Su Dai offered a plan to King Zhao, saying: 'I am willing to risk my life to go to Qin, and with my three-inch tongue that never decays, I will persuade Qin to withdraw its troops.'

[P6] Su Dai arrived in the State of Qin with many gold, silver, and treasures. The king of Qin, King Zhao of Qin, appointed Fan Ju as prime minister and Bai Qi as general, making the state of Qin increasingly powerful. However, Su Dai did not go to seek an audience with King Zhao of Qin to ask him to withdraw from the State of Zhao. Instead, he brought valuable gifts to Fan Ju's prime minister's residence. What did he intend to do?

[P7] Su Dai bowed to Fan Ju and said, 'Bai Qi has won a great victory at Changping, and is now in high spirits. If he captures Handan, he will become the top meritorious official for unifying the Qin Empire!' Upon hearing this, Fan Ju's face turned dark. Su Dai, however, was not afraid at all, and continued, 'I am truly worried about you, Chancellor! Although your current position is higher than Bai Qi's, it won't be long before Bai Qi surpasses you.'

[P8] Fan Ju was very dissatisfied. Although he hadn't gone to the battlefield, he had collected grain and supplies and devised strategies. His contributions were no small matter. How could Bai Qi's rank be higher than his?
After a while, he asked Su Dai, "What good plan do you have?" Su Dai presented the gifts he had brought and said, "Why doesn't the Prime Minister persuade King Qin to withdraw from Handan and make peace with the State of Zhao? That way, Bai Qi won't be able to gain more merit, and your position will be as stable as Mount Tai."

[P9] The next day, Fan Ju said to the King of Qin: "Your Majesty, in the Battle of Changping, we suffered many casualties. It would be better if the two countries stopped fighting for now and let Zhao cede several cities to us. Our soldiers have been fighting for years and are exhausted. Let them return to rest and recuperate!" The King of Qin thought for a moment and said: "After years of warfare, our stored grain and fodder are running low. It would be good to stop fighting now!" He agreed to the truce, accepted the six cities Zhao offered, and then ordered Bai Qi to lead his troops back to Xianyang. Thus, Zhao was saved.

[P10] At this moment, Bai Qi was just about to launch a full-scale attack to conquer the State of Zhao! Suddenly, he received an order to withdraw his troops. He angrily returned to Xianyang. Hearing that Fan Ju had proposed peace talks, Bai Qi glared at him and puffed out his cheeks, deeply hating him.

[P11] The year of the truce was peaceful and prosperous. In autumn, Qin's harvest was bountiful, and their weapons and war chariots had all been repaired. Thus, King Qin wanted to send Bai Qi to attack the State of Zhao again. Bai Qi was ill, yet he still went to the palace to advise the king: 'After we withdrew our troops, Zhao sent envoys with gifts to form alliances with various feudal states. Now they have united and are guarding against us. This battle cannot be won!'

[P12] The King of Qin knew that after Bai Qi withdrew his troops from Handan, he was unhappy. He thought Bai Qi was pretending to be ill and refusing to fight, so he angrily said, "If you Bai Qi don't want to lead the troops, what's there to fear? I have plenty of generals in Qin!" So, he sent another general, Wang Ling, to attack the State of Zhao. Unexpectedly, Wang Ling was truly incompetent in battle. Not only did he fail to win, but his own camp was also broken into by Zhao's army.

[P13] The King of Qin sent Fan Ju to ask Bai Qi to lead the troops. Seeing Fan Ju, Bai Qi was furious: "In the Battle of Changping, we killed 450,000 Zhao soldiers. The Zhao people were terrified. That was the perfect chance to destroy Zhao, yet you advised the King to make peace with Zhao. Now Zhao has raised its city walls, deepened its moats, and expanded its army... Their people and soldiers are united. How can we possibly win? My illness is not yet healed. I cannot fight!"
Hmph!

[P14] Fan Ju returned to the palace and told the King of Qin exactly what Bai Qi had said. The King, upon hearing this, became furious and immediately issued an edict: strip Bai Qi of his official title, demote him to a common soldier, and exile his entire family from Xianyang. Since Bai Qi was ill and unable to move, the King gave him a three-month deadline. Once the three months were up, the King sent people every day to urge Bai Qi to leave.

[P15] In the twelfth month, the city of Xianyang was swept by howling cold winds. Bai Qi, accompanied by two attendants, secretly left the city through the West Gate. Upon hearing this, Fan Ju, worried, told the King of Qin: 'Bai Qi must surely harbor resentment toward Your Majesty. If he leaves Xianyang and defected to another state, he would become a great menace to our Qin state!' The King, upon hearing this, immediately sent a fast horse to catch up with Bai Qi and bestowed upon him a sharp, precious sword.

[P16] When Bai Qi was besieging Handan, Su Dai came to the State of Qin, stoking Fan Ju's jealousy and inciting a rivalry between him and Bai Qi. Fan Ju successfully persuaded King Qin to withdraw troops from Handan, thus relieving the State of Zhao from its immediate crisis and saving it from destruction. Zhao watched as its enemies fought each other, just like standing by the riverbank watching a fire on the opposite shore—doing nothing, yet ultimately reaping benefits. This strategy is called 'Watching the Fire from the Other Shore'.
full_summary_zh:
[P1] 本页展示了成语“隔岸观火”的标题，配图是一位古代人物站在宝箱旁，似乎在策划或观察某事，暗示该成语的含义。
[P2] 清晨，一名骑马的武将急驰进入赵国都城邯郸，城门口的百姓纷纷让路，他直奔王宫而去。
[P3] 画面描绘了赵国百姓在长平之战后悲痛的场景，百姓们唉声叹气，感叹战败，城中哀声不断，反映了战争带来的巨大伤亡和民众的痛苦。
[P4] 传令官向赵王报告秦国武安君白起已攻下17城并逼近邯郸，赵王惊慌失措，担忧国家危在旦夕。
[P5] 赵王召集大臣商议如何应对秦国大军压境，众人束手无策。平原君的门客苏代自告奋勇，表示愿以口才说服秦国退兵。
[P6] 苏代带着金银财宝来到秦国，没有去见秦昭王，而是前往丞相范雎的府邸，引发读者对他意图的好奇。
[P7] 苏代拜访秦国丞相范雎，用激将法暗示白起若攻下邯郸将功高盖主，从而引发范雎的担忧，为后续劝说秦国退兵埋下伏笔。
[P8] 范雎因不满白起功高而心生嫉妒，苏代趁机送上礼物，并建议他劝秦王与赵国议和，以遏制白起的功绩，巩固自身地位。
[P9] 范雎劝说秦王与赵国停战，秦王同意接受赵国割让的六座城池后，让白起撤兵，赵国得以保全。
[P10] 白起在即将攻下赵国时接到撤兵命令，怒气冲冲返回咸阳，得知是范雎提议议和后，对他极为不满。
[P11] 白起虽病重，仍进宫劝谏秦王不要攻打赵国，指出赵国已联合诸侯结盟，秦国若出兵将难以取胜。
[P12] 秦王因白起撤兵而生气，认为其装病推脱，遂派王陵攻打赵国，但王陵战败，军营被赵军攻破。
[P13] 秦王派范雎请白起出战，白起因不满范雎此前劝和而愤怒拒绝，认为赵国已加强防御，且自己病未痊愈，无法出战。
[P14] 范雎将白起的言论如实禀报秦王，秦王大怒，下令削去白起官爵、贬为士兵并驱逐其家族出咸阳，同时限白起三月内离境，逾期则每日派人催促。
[P15] 白起被贬后秘密离开咸阳，范雎担心他投奔敌国，劝说秦王追上他并赐予宝剑，暗示其可能被赐死。
[P16] 本页总结了苏代挑拨范雎与白起关系，导致秦军撤兵，赵国得以保全的历史事件，并解释了“隔岸观火”这一计策的含义。
